html:
The Pale of Settlement was the western region of the Russian Empire, including today's Belarus, Lithuania, Ukraine, Moldova and eastern Poland, where Jews were allowed to live from 1791 to 1917.

Russia took over a huge Jewish population in the partitions of Poland and confined it there. In many Belarusian towns, such as Minsk, Pinsk and Vitebsk, Jews made up half or more of the people, speaking Yiddish and living in shtetls. Poverty, restrictions and pogroms like the Kishinev pogrom drove mass emigration to America from the 1880s. The Pale gave birth to Hasidic and secular Jewish movements, Zionist and socialist alike. It ended with the Russian Revolution, and its Jewish world was destroyed in the Holocaust.
sum: The Pale of Settlement was the western region of the Russian Empire, including today's Belarus, Lithuania, Ukraine, Moldova and eastern Poland, where Jews were allowed to live from 1791 to 1917.
